questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code manages database connections from the pool? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Suppose MaxOpenConns is 10 and all 10 connections are in use when another handler calls QueryContext. What happens to that call?
choices: It opens an 11th connection because MaxIdleConns allows it.
It returns an error immediately with a 'too many connections' message.
It waits for a connection to be released until its context is done, then fails with the context's error.
It runs on one of the busy connections at the same time.

questions.prompt: What does g.SetLimit(4) in ForAdvertisers accomplish for the connection pool?
choices: It caps the number of rows fetched per advertiser at four.
It retries each failed advertiser query up to four times.
It limits the pool to four connections for the whole process.
It bounds one report request to at most four concurrent queries, so one large request cannot take every connection.

questions.prompt: Why does RecordBatch call `defer tx.Rollback()` even though it ends with tx.Commit()?
choices: Rollback after a successful Commit undoes the inserts, so it must be removed.
If any step returns early, the deferred Rollback releases the transaction's connection back to the pool; after a successful Commit it returns sql.ErrTxDone and does nothing.
Commit alone does not release the connection, only Rollback does.
It is required for ON CONFLICT upserts to be applied.
